evidence.label: Fiber functors for finite symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic

headline: Every finite symmetric tensor category in characteristic p is claimed to map into one higher Verlinde category.
scope: Finite symmetric tensor categories over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, including p = 2.
plain: A symmetric tensor category is an abstract setting with objects that combine and can swap order. Benson, Etingof and Ostrik built a tower of model categories, the higher Verlinde categories. They conjectured every reasonable category maps faithfully into this tower. This paper claims to prove it for every finite such category, in every characteristic p > 0. The level of the tower used may depend on the category.
doesNot: This does not cover symmetric tensor categories that are not finite, which the full conjecture also includes.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Dave Benson, Pavel Etingof and Victor Ostrik, the higher Verlinde conjecture
scorecard.significanceWhy: It would settle the finite case of the main structural conjecture for symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic.

explanation:
Work with arithmetic mod 5, where 5 counts as 0. Take the 3-by-3 matrix with 1s on the diagonal and 1s just above it. Raised to the fifth power it gives the identity, so it describes an action of a five-element cycle. Such a matrix is called a Jordan block of length 3. Now combine two copies into one 9-by-9 matrix, the tensor product. Computing its block structure mod 5 gives blocks of lengths 1, 3 and 5.

The block of length 5 is special. In a precise sense it is negligible, and one can throw it away. Keeping only blocks of lengths 1 to 4 gives a small world in which 3 times 3 is 1 plus 3. In the same world, 4 times 4 leaves only 1, since the rest is three blocks of length 5. This world is the first Verlinde category for the prime 5[1,2]. For the prime 2 it is ordinary vector spaces, and for 3 it is supervector spaces[3].

A symmetric tensor category is an abstract setting with objects, a way to combine them, and a rule for swapping the order. Representations of a group are the basic example. A fiber functor is a faithful translation from one such setting into another that keeps all this structure[4]. Over the complex numbers, Deligne showed in 2002 that supervector spaces are a common target for every reasonable category of this kind[5]. In positive characteristic p, that fails. Ostrik proved that the semisimple ones, called fusion categories, translate into the first Verlinde category[6]. Benson, Etingof and Ostrik then built a tower of higher Verlinde categories, one level for each power of p[2]. They conjectured that every reasonable symmetric tensor category translates into this tower[7].

This paper claims to prove that conjecture for every finite symmetric tensor category[8]. That includes characteristic two[8]. The level of the tower may depend on the category[9]. Finite here means finitely many basic objects, finite-dimensional spaces of maps, and enough projective objects[10]. The paper makes no claim about larger categories that are not finite[9].

The single obstacle is that the natural translation tool can fail. It is called the Frobenius functor, and it need not be exact, meaning it can break short sequences of objects[11]. Higher versions of it, built by Coulembier and Flake, become usable once a specific conjecture about tilting modules holds[12]. The paper claims to prove that conjecture in full[13]. It then picks a version of the higher functor that is exact for the given category. A counting argument with dimensions finishes the descent into one level of the tower.

The result also classifies the finite categories that cannot be compressed further[14]. These are the ones where every structure-preserving translation out of them is faithful on maps.

How sure is this? There is no Lean formalization for this result in the openai/math release, so no computer has checked the proof. The argument builds on a large body of recent work on Verlinde categories and Frobenius functors. No specialist review of the paper has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if it holds. There is no Lean check, it rests on recent heavy machinery, and no specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: A square matrix with one repeated value on the diagonal and 1s just above it.
An abstract setting of objects and maps with a way to combine objects and swap their order.
A faithful, exact translation between two such settings that keeps combining and swapping intact.
A model category built from Jordan blocks after throwing away negligible pieces; higher levels form a tower.
Arithmetic where adding 1 to itself p times gives 0.
A translation that sends short exact sequences of objects to short exact sequences.
A tool that raises structure to the p-th power; it can fail to be exact.
